title: Connected top-conductor bound for the binary Hayes identity class
statement: Let ell >= 200, let n be 2 ell + 1 or 2 ell + 2, put L=ceil(log_2 ell)+1 and a=ell-L, and let N_j(1) be the degree-n Mangoldt population in the identity class of the level-j binary Hayes quotient. Then the absolute value of 2^ell N_ell(1) - 2^(a-1) N_(a-1)(1) is at most 2^(2 ell - 2).

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; connected identity-path refinement of the binary Hayes class distribution

notes: This is one uniform analytic obligation, not a finite computation result. The left side is exactly the signed sum of all weighted Haar increments from level a through ell and, equivalently, the degree-n Mangoldt trace over the union of those exact-conductor character families. It is also the relative point trace #C_ell(GF(2^n)) - #C_(a-1)(GF(2^n)) for the binary Carlitz cyclotomic tower. The CAS checks the fine/coarse telescope, the quadratic Artin-Schreier step count, the Galois-degree product, and that the relative genus reproduces the separate top-level Weil envelope. The standard individual Weil estimate proves that all lower levels contribute less than 2^(2 ell - 1); therefore this quarter-scale connected bound implies the required endpoint discrepancy with reserve for every ell>=200. At ell=200 the connected window is j=191,...,200, and the required saving over relative Hasse-Weil is exactly 50641/32, with integral ceiling 1583. Both endpoint traces satisfy the candidate in exact fleet runs for every 16<=ell<=20; at ell=20 their absolute candidate-normalized ratios are approximately 0.0087 and 0.0227. Finite survival and an exact geometric representation are not theorem evidence for the bound. No proof operation is registered.
